translation_en: 'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to us: Mansur informed us, with this chain, with the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both from 'Abd al-A'la. Ibn al-Muthanna said: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Hittan ibn 'Abdullah al-Raqashi, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: When revelation came to Allah's Prophet, he was distressed by it and his face became troubled. One day revelation came to him in this state. When it had passed, he said: Take it from me, for Allah has made a way for them: a previously married woman with a previously married man, and a virgin with a virgin. The previously married are to receive one hundred lashes and then be stoned; the virgins are to receive one hundred lashes and then exile for a year.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to me. Both reported from Qatadah with this chain. Their wording says, The virgin is flogged and exiled, and the previously married person is flogged and stoned. They did not mention a year or one hundred lashes.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah informed me that he heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas say: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said while seated on the Messenger of Allah's pulpit: Allah sent Muhammad with the truth and revealed the Book to him. Among what was revealed to him was the verse of stoning. We recited it, understood it, and retained it. The Messenger of Allah stoned, and we stoned after him. I fear that as time passes someone will say, We do not find stoning in Allah's Book, and they will go astray by abandoning an obligation Allah revealed. Stoning in Allah's Book is a truth for a man or woman who commits adultery after being married, when proof is established, pregnancy occurs, or there is a confession.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us; they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, with this chain.

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to me: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, who said: 'Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A Muslim man came to the Messenger of Allah while he was in the mosque, called to him, and said, Messenger of Allah, I have committed adultery. He turned away. The man moved in front of him and repeated it; the Prophet turned away. He did this four times. When he had testified against himself four times, the Messenger of Allah called him and asked whether he was insane. He said no. The Prophet asked whether he had been married, and he said yes. The Messenger of Allah said, Take him and stone him.

Ibn Shihab said: Someone who heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah informed me that he said: I was among those who stoned him. We stoned him at the prayer ground. When the stones hurt him, he fled, and we caught him at al-Harrah and stoned him.

Al-Layth also narrated it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn Musafir, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain, with the like of it. 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated this to me: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, with this chain as well. Both reports say Ibn Shihab informed me that someone who heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah said what 'Uqayl related.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me. Another chain: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar and Ibn Jurayj informed us, all from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, from the Prophet, with a report like 'Uqayl's narration from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id and Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah.

Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn al-Jahdari narrated to me: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: I saw Ma'iz ibn Malik when he was brought to the Prophet. He was a short, stocky man without an outer garment. He testified against himself four times that he had committed adultery. The Messenger of Allah said, Perhaps you only... He replied, No, by Allah, I really committed adultery. The Prophet had him stoned. Then he addressed the people: Whenever we set out to fight in Allah's way, one of you stays behind with a billy-goat-like bleat, giving one of them a little milk. By Allah, if I gain power over one of them, I will punish him severely for it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us. The wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's. They said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: my father narrated to us, both from Simak ibn Harb, who said he heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: A short, unkempt, muscular man wearing a waist wrapper who had committed adultery was brought to the Messenger of Allah. He turned him away twice, then ordered that he be stoned. The Messenger of Allah said: Whenever we set out to fight in Allah's way, one of you stays behind bleating like a billy goat, giving one of them a little milk. If Allah gives me power over one of them, I will make him an example, or punish him severely. Simak said: I told this to Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said the Prophet turned him away four times.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Shababah narrated to us. Another chain: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi narrated to us. Both reported from Shu'bah, from Simak, from Jabir ibn Samurah, from the Prophet, with a report like Ibn Ja'far's. Shababah agreed that he turned him away twice. Abu 'Amir's report says twice or three times.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us. The wording is Qutaybah's. They said: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet said to Ma'iz ibn Malik: Is what I have heard about you true? He asked what had been heard. The Prophet said he had heard that he had been intimate with so-and-so's servant girl. He said yes. He testified four times, then the Prophet ordered that he be stoned.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me: Dawud narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, that a man from Aslam called Ma'iz ibn Malik came to the Messenger of Allah and said, I have committed an immoral act, so carry out the prescribed punishment on me. The Prophet turned him away several times. Then he asked his people, and they said they knew nothing wrong with him except that he had done something he thought only the punishment could expiate. He returned to the Prophet, who ordered us to stone him. We took him to al-Baqi'. We did not tie him up or dig a pit. We threw bones, clods, and pottery at him. He ran, and we pursued him until he reached the edge of al-Harrah. He stood there, and we threw large stones at him until he was still. That evening the Messenger of Allah stood and addressed the people: Whenever we set out to fight in Allah's way, a man stays behind among our families bleating like a billy goat. I pledge that if such a man is brought to me, I will punish him severely. He neither asked forgiveness for Ma'iz nor insulted him.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us: Dawud narrated to us with this chain, with the same meaning. This report says that the Prophet stood in the evening, praised Allah, and said: What is the matter with people that whenever we go on an expedition, one of them stays behind, bleating like a billy goat? It does not say among our families.

Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us. Both reported from Dawud with this chain, part of the hadith. Sufyan's report says he confessed to adultery three times.

Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' al-Hamdani narrated to us: Yahya ibn Ya'la, al-Harithi al-Muharibi, narrated to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jami' al-Muharibi, from 'Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father: Ma'iz ibn Malik came to the Prophet and said, Messenger of Allah, purify me. He said, Woe to you, go back, ask Allah's forgiveness, and repent to Him. Ma'iz returned shortly afterward and repeated his request. The Prophet again told him to go back, ask forgiveness, and repent. This happened again. On the fourth time, the Messenger of Allah asked, From what should I purify you? He said, From adultery. The Prophet asked whether he was insane. He was told he was not. He asked whether he had drunk wine. A man smelled his breath and found no smell of wine. The Messenger of Allah asked, Did you commit adultery? He said yes, so the Prophet ordered him stoned. People divided: some said he was doomed and his sin had encompassed him; others said no repentance was better than Ma'iz's, who came to the Prophet, placed his hand in the Prophet's hand, and asked to be killed with stones. They remained in this discussion two or three days. Then the Messenger of Allah came while they sat, greeted them, and sat down. He said, Ask Allah to forgive Ma'iz ibn Malik. They said, May Allah forgive Ma'iz ibn Malik. The Messenger of Allah said, He has repented with a repentance that, if divided among a whole community, would suffice them. Then a woman from Ghamid of Azd came and said, Messenger of Allah, purify me. He told her to go back, ask Allah's forgiveness, and repent. She said, Do you intend to send me back as you sent Ma'iz back? He asked what was the matter. She said she was pregnant from adultery. He told her to wait until she gave birth. A man from the Ansar cared for her until she delivered, then told the Prophet. He said, Then we cannot stone her and leave her infant with no one to nurse him. A man from the Ansar offered to nurse the child. The Prophet then had her stoned.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us; the two wordings are close. My father narrated to us: Bashir ibn al-Muhajir narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Buraydah narrated to us, from his father: Ma'iz ibn Malik al-Aslami came to the Messenger of Allah and said, I have wronged myself and committed adultery; I want you to purify me. The Prophet turned him away. The next day he came and repeated that he had committed adultery, and the Prophet turned him away a second time. The Messenger of Allah sent for his people and asked if they knew any defect in his mind or found anything objectionable in him. They said they knew him to be sound-minded and among the best of them as far as they knew. He came a third time, and the Prophet asked them about him again; they said there was nothing wrong with him or his mind. The fourth time, the Prophet had a pit dug for him and ordered him stoned. Then the Ghamidi woman came and said she had committed adultery and wanted purification. He turned her away. The next day she asked why he sent her back and said she was pregnant. He told her to go until she gave birth. After she delivered, she brought the child wrapped in cloth. He told her to nurse him until weaning. When she had weaned him, she brought him with a piece of bread in his hand and said he had been weaned and was eating food. The Prophet entrusted the child to a Muslim man, then had a pit dug for her up to her chest and ordered the people to stone her. Khalid ibn al-Walid threw a stone that struck her head, and blood splashed on his face. He insulted her. The Prophet heard him and said, Take it easy, Khalid. By the One in whose hand is my soul, she has repented with a repentance that, if a tax collector repented with it, he would be forgiven. Then he ordered that she be prayed over, and she was buried.

Abu Ghassan Malik ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Misma'i narrated to me: Mu'adh, meaning Ibn Hisham, narrated to us: my father narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir: Abu Qilabah narrated to me that Abu al-Muhallab told him, from 'Imran ibn Husayn: A woman from Juhaynah came to the Prophet of Allah pregnant from adultery and said, Prophet of Allah, I have incurred a prescribed punishment, so carry it out on me. The Prophet summoned her guardian and said, Treat her well; when she gives birth, bring her to me. He did so. The Prophet ordered that her clothes be secured around her, then that she be stoned. He prayed over her. 'Umar asked, Do you pray over her when she committed adultery? He said, She has repented with a repentance that, if divided among seventy people of Madinah, would suffice them. Have you found a better repentance than her giving herself for Allah Most High?
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us: Aban al-'Attar narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, with this chain, with the like of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Abu Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, who said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah and said, I adjure you by Allah to judge between us according to Allah's Book. The other litigant, who was more learned than he, said, Yes, judge between us according to Allah's Book, and allow me to speak. The Messenger of Allah said, Speak. He said: My son worked for this man and committed adultery with his wife. I was told that my son was to be stoned, so I ransomed him for one hundred sheep and a female servant. I asked learned people, who told me my son must receive one hundred lashes and exile for a year, while this man's wife must be stoned. The Messenger of Allah said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, I will judge between you according to Allah's Book. The servant and sheep are returned. Your son receives one hundred lashes and exile for a year. Go tomorrow, Unays, to this man's wife; if she confesses, stone her. He went to her, she confessed, and the Messenger of Allah ordered that she be stoned.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me. Another chain: 'Amr al-Naqid narrated to me: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih. Another chain: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar. All of them reported from al-Zuhri with this chain, with the like of it.

Al-Hakam ibn Musa Abu Salih narrated to me: Shu'ayb ibn Ishaq narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah informed us, from Nafi', that 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar informed him: The Messenger of Allah was brought a Jewish man and woman who had committed adultery. He went to the Jews and asked, What do you find in the Torah for one who commits adultery? They said, We blacken their faces, make them ride facing backward, and parade them. He said, Bring the Torah if you are truthful. They brought it and recited it. When they reached the verse of stoning, the young man reading put his hand over it and read what came before and after. 'Abdullah ibn Salam, who was with the Messenger of Allah, told him to ask the man to lift his hand. He lifted it, and beneath it was the verse of stoning. The Messenger of Allah ordered them both stoned. Ibn 'Umar said: I was among those who stoned them, and I saw the man shield her from the stones with himself.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Isma'il, meaning Ibn 'Ulayyah, narrated to us, from Ayyub. Another chain: Abu al-Tahir informed me: 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: men of knowledge, including Malik ibn Anas, informed me that Nafi' informed them, from Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah stoned two Jews, a man and a woman, who had committed adultery. The Jews brought them to the Messenger of Allah, and they related the hadith in a similar manner.

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Jews brought to the Messenger of Allah a man and woman from among them who had committed adultery. He related the hadith like the report of 'Ubaydullah from Nafi'.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, both from Abu Mu'awiyah. Yahya said: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from al-A'mash, from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib: A Jew whose face had been blackened and who had been flogged passed by the Prophet. He called them and asked, Is this the prescribed punishment for adultery that you find in your Book? They said yes. He summoned one of their scholars and adjured him by Allah who revealed the Torah to Moses: Is this what you find in your Book? He said no; had you not adjured me in this way, I would not have told you. We find stoning there, but it became common among our nobles, so when we caught a noble we let him go, and when we caught a weak person we carried out the punishment. We agreed to apply one punishment to noble and low alike, so we substituted blackening the face and flogging for stoning. The Messenger of Allah said, O Allah, I am the first to revive Your command after they had let it die. He ordered the man stoned. Then Allah, Mighty and Exalted, revealed the verses in al-Ma'idah 5:41 beginning, O Messenger, do not grieve over those who hasten into disbelief, through the words, If you are given this, accept it. This means: Bring it to Muhammad; if he orders blackening and flogging, accept it, but if he gives the ruling of stoning, beware. Allah also revealed the verses 5:44, 5:45, and 5:47: Whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers, the wrongdoers, and the defiantly disobedient, concerning the disbelievers.

Ibn Numayr and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us with this chain, with the like of it up to the words that the Prophet ordered him stoned. He did not mention what followed about the revelation of the verse.

Harun ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say: The Prophet stoned a man from Aslam and a Jewish man and his wife.
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us with this chain, with the like of it, except that he said, and a woman.

Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us: Sulayman al-Shaybani narrated to us, who said: I asked 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—the wording is his—'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, who said: I asked 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa whether the Messenger of Allah stoned. He said yes. I asked whether that was after Surat al-Nur was revealed or before it. He said, I do not know.
